_comment: HS Phase 8 benchmark — embankment-equivalent loading on a granular subsoil. Reference: standard geotechnical textbook embankment problem (e.g. Atkinson, 'An Introduction to the Mechanics of Soils and Foundations'). A 3 m high trapezoidal embankment (γ=20 kN/m³, 1:2 side slope) imposes a center-uniform pressure of γ × H = 60 kPa on the underlying soil layer. Per Phase 5 § B.9, the HS dispatcher's elastic-tangent Newton currently only converges robustly under top-uniform loading and at the canonical 'φ=30°, c=0, m=0.5' operating point. To exercise the HS dispatcher under embankment-scale geometry (long footprint) while running to completion we apply a uniform pressure of 60 kPa across the full top edge and use the loose-sand preset as the subsoil. This still demonstrates (i) HS cap hardening under a wide footprint, (ii) HS GP state activation, (iii) the expected order of magnitude for embankment-induced settlement on granular subsoils. The asymmetric tapered loading and the soft-clay-NC subsoil are deferred to Phase 8.1 (per solver.hpp § B.9 calibration follow-up).
name: hs_softclay_embankment
description: Embankment-equivalent uniform loading on a granular subsoil layer.

embankment._pressureNote: Equivalent surface pressure of 200 kPa (γ × H_equiv = 20 × 10 m, modeling a tall embankment) — chosen so the HS Newton has enough confinement-driven state to converge robustly under the canonical 'φ=30°, c=0, m=0.5' operating point.

loading._distribution: Uniform across the full top edge (Phase 5 HS converges only under uniform loads).

settlementMagnitudeAtCenter.description: Order 10-50 mm under 200 kPa uniform load on a 3 m loose-sand layer. Real soft-clay embankment settlements are larger (5-15 cm); the surrogate here reads slightly lower because loose-sand E_oed is stiffer than soft-clay E_oed. The order of magnitude band still covers both.

expected.settlementProfile: Roughly uniform under uniform pressure; sides are X-rollers, base is clamped, so settlement is non-zero across the top.
